items.a: A Next.js 16 / React 19 boilerplate focused on SEO and AI, deployable on Netlify, with an isolated component library (Material UI) and OpenRouter wiring through a Route Handler.
The default model is a free OpenRouter model (openrouter/free). A daily quota limits browser calls; errors surface as toasts so you can retry easily.
No. Theme, cookie consent and the daily counter are stored locally (cookie + localStorage). The OpenRouter key stays server‑side and is never exposed to the browser.

items.q: How do I add a new AI action?
items.a: Drop a file in capabilities/agents/ (or a folder capabilities/skills/<id>/), then call POST /api/run with { prompt, agentId?, skillId?, inputs? }. The route stays thin: composition, quota, timeout and errors live in lib/ai (run → composeRun + runPrompt).

items.q: Is the site indexable by Google?
items.a: Yes: server rendering, localized URLs, metadata, hreflang, XML sitemap and an HTML sitemap are provided.

about.title: About
about.intro: Yoann Barbier, freelance full-stack developer in Nantes, France, since 2021: React, TypeScript, Node.js, and author of the open-source Axons boilerplate.
about.lead: A freelance full-stack developer in Nantes since 2021, I design and evolve web applications with React, TypeScript and Node.js. I am the author of Axons, the open-source Next.js boilerplate this site is built on.
summary: Author of the open-source Axons boilerplate.
Based in Nantes, available remotely or on site depending on the project.
approach: I work mainly with JavaScript and TypeScript, with particular attention to code quality, performance and the robustness of the solutions.
I like understanding and solving problems, algorithmic ones in particular: I took part in the TopCoder Open marathons, just for the fun of it.
background: CTO of Keople (myKeople SaaS HR platform) from 2014 to 2018, then full-stack lead developer from 2018 to 2021.

services.title: Services

siteHome.lead: A freelance full-stack developer in Nantes, I build and evolve websites and web applications in JavaScript and TypeScript, now with the help of AI. I pay close attention to code quality, tests and the reliability of what I deliver.
approach: Understand a problem before solving it, and look for the simplest solution that holds up.
Plan ahead rather than react: set a clear context from the start, to avoid last-minute changes.
Do things properly, even if it takes a little longer, so there is less to come back to later.
Develop with AI (Claude Code, local models) while keeping control of quality, tests and technical choices.
Algorithm and optimisation problems, like those of the TopCoder Open, with approaches such as simulated annealing or beam search.
